items.title: FinAgent
items.text:
FinAgent is a local-first personal finance agent. It imports your bank and credit-card statements, categorizes every transaction with rules, location lookup, and a local LLM, and renders everything in a dashboard that runs on your own machine.

Nothing leaves your computer. No cloud accounts, no telemetry, no data uploads.

items.title: Where to go
items.text: Topic Page Run the shortest command for any platform Quick start Detailed native and Docker setup Installation What happens the first time you launch First-run setup Getting statements into FinAgent Importing statements How processing works, progress, and dates Processing pipeline Every terminal flag and utility Running from the terminal Stop / restart the app cleanly Restarting FinAgent Personal vs. Dev profile Profiles Every config key explained Configuration reference The category system and rule engine Categories & rules

items.title: The short version
items.text:
1. Launch FinAgent. On first run the dashboard opens on the Settings page.
  2. Complete setup — choose your statements and processing folders, pick an LLM provider and a location-lookup method, then press Complete setup.
  3. Import statements on the Import page. Use a CSV or supported tabular text export from your bank — PDF statements are not supported.
  4. Process them on the Process page — a run button with live progress.
  5. Explore the Overview, Monthly, Transactions, and Budget pages.

Start with Quick start, then use Installation for platform details, providers, Docker persistence, updates, and troubleshooting.

items.title: The category system
items.text:
Categories are two-level: group:subcategory (e.g. housing:rent_mortgage). The canonical list lives in a reference CSV shipped with the app and is shown on the dashboard's Categories page with readable names and emojis.

The set is deliberately closed: rules, location lookup, and the LLM prompt are all tuned against it. Adding categories is highly discouraged — it fragments your history and new categories only apply going forward.

If you must add one (Dev profile only, via the Categories page):

  • The group must be one of the existing groups.
  • The subcategory is free-form; it is slugified to lower_snake_case.
  • The reference CSV and the dynamic category store are both updated.

items.title: The rule engine
items.text:
Rules run first in the pipeline — before location lookup and the LLM — and are deterministic keyword matches against transaction descriptions.

Manage rules on the Rule Engine page:

  • Create, edit, reorder (priority), and delete rules.
  • Rules created from the dashboard are stored in rules_dynamic.json and survive app updates.
  • The rule suggester can propose rules from your uncategorized transactions.

items.title: Editing a single transaction
items.text: Use the edit button on any row of the Transactions page. Manual edits are recorded with the user_defined stage (orange tag) and are preserved across processing runs.

items.title: Configuration reference
items.text: Personal config lives at ~/.finagent/config.json and Dev config normally lives at ~/.finagent-dev/config.json. Override the active directory with the FINAGENT_CONFIG_DIR environment variable. Edit the selected profile through the dashboard's Settings page, the terminal wizard (finagent --setup), or by hand.

items.title: Keys
items.text: Key Values Notes statements_dir path Raw statements root. Locked after setup — rerun finagent --setup to change. processing_dir path Pipeline output + dashboard data. Locked after setup. llm_provider ollama · open_router · claude · none Categorization engine (setup guide). llm_model model name e.g. llama3.1:8b for Ollama. ollama_model model name Ollama only. Default qwen2.5:3b; must already be pulled (ollama pull <model>), e.g. qwen3. ollama_api_url URL Ollama only. Default http://localhost:11434. openrouter_api_key string Only for the OpenRouter provider. Free to generate at openrouter.ai/keys. claude_api_key string Only for the Claude provider. Default claude-opus-4-5. location_lookup_method nominatim · google_maps · combined · place_api · place_api_combined · none Personal supports nominatim, both Place API modes, and none. items.text: Port Serves dashboard_port The dashboard (production) dashboard_port + 1 API server (dev mode only) dashboard_port + 2 This documentation site

items.title: Importing statements
items.text:
The Import page accepts CSV or supported tabular text statement exports from your banks.

PDF statements are not supported

On your bank's download/export screen, choose CSV, comma-separated, or a supported tabular text format. Do not download or upload a PDF: a PDF is a visual document, not the transaction table FinAgent needs. Bank of America checking .txt exports are converted to CSV automatically.

items.title: Supported banks
items.text: Bank Folder Accounts American Express AMEX Credit Bank of America BOA Checking, Credit Chase CHASE Checking, Credit Citi CITI Credit US Bank USBANK Checking, Credit

items.title: How to import
items.text:
1. Download a CSV or supported tabular text export from your bank's website — not a PDF.
  2. On the Import page, select the bank and complete each field marked *: account type and account last four digits.
  3. Optionally enter an account label using letters and numbers. FinAgent saves it for later imports. If left blank, FinAgent creates a reusable five-digit label or reuses the matching bank/type/last-four account.
  4. Statement dates are optional, but enter both when using them. Dates use YYYYMMDD (for example, January 31, 2026 is 20260131). Blank dates receive a unique range beginning at 19000101; later blank imports continue after that account's previous automatic end date to prevent filename collisions.
  5. Choose the downloaded file. FinAgent renames it consistently and files it into the correct folder under your statements directory.
  6. Repeat for as many statements as you like.
  7. Press Run processing — the button activates as soon as at least one statement is present — to jump to the Process page.

items.title: Importing by hand
items.text: You can also drop files directly into the statements folders, e.g. <statements>/BOA/CheckingAC/. FinAgent picks them up on the next processing run.

items.title: Installation
items.text: FinAgent ships as a standalone binary — no Python required for normal use. Pick your platform below. For commands only, see Quick start.

items.title: Docker installation
items.text: The Docker release contains the packaged FinAgent binary, dashboard, documentation, Node.js, and Ollama. It does not contain the private source tree or raw Python source files.

items.title: Docker requirements
items.text:
• Docker Desktop, or Docker Engine with Docker Compose.
  • FinAgent-Docker-x86_64.tar.gz, docker_up.sh, and docker-compose.yml from the same release, kept in one folder.
  • Two host folders: one for statements and one for processing output.

items.title: Load and start the image
items.text:
1. Load the release image and make the launcher executable:

    docker load -i FinAgent-Docker-x86_64.tar.gz
chmod +x docker_up.sh

  2. Start without downloading an LLM model:

    ./docker_up.sh \
   --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
   --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing" \
   --no-ollama-model

  3. Open the dashboard at http://localhost:3001 and documentation at http://localhost:3003.

The launcher creates missing host folders. Settings displays mounted paths as Docker-locked so every component continues using the same persistent folders.

Preview before starting

Add --dry-run to print the Compose command, ports, mounts, provider, and model choice without opening a container.

items.title: Docker ports
items.text:
The dashboard defaults to host port 3001. Documentation defaults to the dashboard port plus 2, so it normally uses 3003.

./docker_up.sh \
   --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
   --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing" \
   --port 4100 \
   --docs-port 4200 \
   --no-ollama-model

Both ports must be different whole numbers from 1024 through 65535. The dashboard port must be 65533 or lower because FinAgent reserves its internal documentation port. Invalid values are rejected before Docker starts.

items.title: Ollama in Docker
items.text:
Ollama is always installed in the image. Model downloads are optional and are stored in the persistent ollama-data volume.

# Pull and select the small default model: qwen2.5:0.5b
./docker_up.sh --ollama-model \
   --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
   --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing"

# Pull and select another model
./docker_up.sh --ollama-model qwen2.5:3b \
   --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
   --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing"

# Skip model download
./docker_up.sh --no-ollama-model \
   --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
   --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing"

With neither model flag, an interactive terminal asks whether to download qwen2.5:0.5b; unattended runs do not prompt or download. An explicit model choice becomes the active model shown in Settings and overrides an older model in mounted config for that launch. A restart without an explicit provider or model preserves values previously saved in Settings.

items.title: Claude or OpenRouter in Docker
items.text:
Cloud providers require no additional container software. Keep keys out of shell history by using a local permission-restricted environment file.

ClaudeOpenRouter 
mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/finagent"
printf '%s\n' 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your-key' > "$HOME/.config/finagent/docker.env"
chmod 600 "$HOME/.config/finagent/docker.env"

./docker_up.sh --llm-provider claude \
   --env-file "$HOME/.config/finagent/docker.env" \
   --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
   --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing"

mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/finagent"
printf '%s\n' 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=your-key' > "$HOME/.config/finagent/docker.env"
chmod 600 "$HOME/.config/finagent/docker.env"

./docker_up.sh --llm-provider open_router \
   --env-file "$HOME/.config/finagent/docker.env" \
   --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
   --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing"

The env file accepts only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENROUTER_API_KEY. Keys are injected at startup, masked in the dashboard, and never copied into the image. Providers can also be changed in Settings → Categorization engine.

items.title: Docker data and persistence
items.text:
Data Storage Persists after restart? Imported statements Host --statements folder Yes Processing and dashboard data Host --processing folder Yes FinAgent settings Host --config folder (default .docker-config) Yes Ollama models Docker volume ollama-data Yes

The container restarts automatically unless explicitly stopped.

items.title: Check, restart, and stop Docker
items.text:
docker ps --filter name=finagent
docker logs finagent
curl http://localhost:3001/api/config

docker restart finagent
docker compose --project-name finagent down

Run ./docker_up.sh again to recreate a stopped container with the mounts, ports, and provider options you want.

items.title: Update the Docker release
items.text:
1. Download the new image archive and matching launcher files.
  2. Run docker compose --project-name finagent down.
  3. Run docker load -i FinAgent-Docker-x86_64.tar.gz.
  4. Start again with ./docker_up.sh and your normal options.

Mounted data, config, and the Ollama model volume remain available when the container is replaced.

items.title: Docker troubleshooting
items.text:
• Invalid port: choose different ports from 1024 through 65535; keep the dashboard port at 65533 or lower.
  • Cloud key missing: pass the provider key through --env-file or save it from Settings.
  • Ollama model unavailable: restart with --ollama-model or --ollama-model <name>.
  • Image not loaded: run docker load -i FinAgent-Docker-x86_64.tar.gz.
  • All launcher options: run ./docker_up.sh --help.

items.title: macOS installation
items.text:
1. Download the latest FinAgent-<version>-macOS.dmg from the GitHub releases page.

  2. Install: open the DMG and drag FinAgent.app into Applications.

  3. First launch — approve the security check. Development builds are not notarized with a paid Apple Developer ID, so macOS Gatekeeper may say Apple could not verify that FinAgent is free of malware and offer to move it to the Trash. Approval is needed once per install/update. Ad-hoc signing does not remove the warning for downloaded apps; avoiding it requires Apple notarization and a paid Apple Developer account. Use one of these approval methods:

    • Right-click (or Control-click) FinAgent.app → Open → Open.
    • If macOS still refuses ("Apple could not verify…"), go to System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll to the Security section, and click "Open Anyway" next to the FinAgent message, then confirm with your password or Touch ID.
    • For a release downloaded from the official FinAgent Releases page that you trust, Terminal can remove the quarantine flag with xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/FinAgent.app.

  4. Launch. Double-clicking FinAgent.app opens a Terminal window, starts the app, and opens your browser on the dashboard. First run walks you through setup.

The macOS app includes the dashboard runtime. You do not need to install Node.js or Python separately.

items.title: Set up the finagent terminal alias (macOS)
items.text:
The docs and dashboard refer to the finagent command. The binary lives inside the app bundle, so add an alias to your shell profile:

# zsh (default on modern macOS)
echo 'alias finagent="/Applications/FinAgent.app/Contents/MacOS/finagent"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc

# bash
echo 'alias finagent="/Applications/FinAgent.app/Contents/MacOS/finagent"' >> ~/.bash_profile
source ~/.bash_profile

Verify it works:

finagent --version

The wrapper at Contents/MacOS/finagent detects how it was invoked: from a shell it runs inline (all terminal flags work as expected); from Finder it opens Terminal.app for you.

items.title: Linux installation
items.text:
1. Install Node.js (required for the dashboard). FinAgent launches a Node.js server for the dashboard, so node must be on your PATH first:

    # Debian/Ubuntu — NodeSource LTS repo (gives a current version; the
# distro-packaged "nodejs" apt package is often too old)
curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | sudo -E bash -
sudo apt-get install -y nodejs

# Fedora/RHEL
sudo dnf install -y nodejs

# Arch
sudo pacman -S nodejs npm

    Verify with node --version (v18+; v20 LTS recommended). 2. Download the Linux archive from the releases page and extract it:

    tar -xzf FinAgent-<version>-linux.tar.gz -C ~/finagent

  2. Make the command available on your PATH (pick one):

    # symlink (recommended)
sudo ln -s ~/finagent/finagent /usr/local/bin/finagent

# or shell alias
echo 'alias finagent="$HOME/finagent/finagent"' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc

  3. Run finagent — the dashboard opens in your default browser. If your distribution blocks the binary, mark it executable first: chmod +x ~/finagent/finagent.

items.title: Windows installation
items.text:
1. Download FinAgent-<version>-Windows-x64.exe from the releases page.
  2. Run the installer. It includes the dashboard runtime and creates Start Menu shortcuts; a desktop shortcut is optional. No separate Python or Node.js installation is required.
  3. If SmartScreen displays "Windows protected your PC", click More info → Run anyway.
  4. Leave Launch FinAgent selected on the final page. The browser opens to first-run setup. Later, use the Start Menu or desktop shortcut.

If installation fails unexpectedly, FinAgent writes a short, non-secret diagnostic file in the Windows temporary folder and opens a pre-filled GitHub issue for your review. It includes the FinAgent and Windows versions; attach the installer log only if a maintainer requests it.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Linux only: Node.js 18+ on PATH (20 LTS recommended). macOS and Windows releases include the dashboard runtime; Docker includes all runtimes and Ollama.
  • A categorization engine is optional: Ollama, OpenRouter, Claude, or none for rules and location lookup only.
  • ~500 MB disk for the app plus processed data. Allow additional space for local Ollama models.

items.title: Setting up an LLM provider
items.text: FinAgent uses an LLM to categorize transactions its rule engine can't classify on its own. You choose the provider during first-run setup (or later on the Settings page / finagent --setup). Pick one of the three:

items.title: Option A — Ollama (local, free, private, recommended)
items.text:
Runs entirely on your machine — transaction descriptions never leave your computer, and there's no API key or bill.

  1. Install Ollama:

    • macOS: download from ollama.com/download and drag it to Applications, or brew install ollama.
    • Windows: download the installer from ollama.com/download and run it. Ollama installs itself as a background service with a system-tray icon.

    • Linux:

      curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh

    Ollama starts automatically after install and listens on http://localhost:11434. Verify with:

    ollama --version

  2. Pull a default model. FinAgent's built-in default is the small qwen2.5:3b, but the newer Qwen 3 family is a great free default — fast, accurate enough for categorization, and light on RAM:

    ollama pull qwen3

    On a machine with limited RAM (≤8 GB), use the smaller tag instead:

    ollama pull qwen3:4b

  3. Point FinAgent at the model. In FinAgent's Settings page, choose Ollama as the LLM backend and set the Ollama model field to the tag you pulled (e.g. qwen3 or qwen3:4b). From the terminal wizard, the same prompt is called "Ollama model name".

  4. Verify it works:

    ollama list          # confirms the model was downloaded
ollama run qwen3 "hi" # quick smoke test

items.title: Option B — OpenRouter (cloud API — free to get a key)
items.text:
OpenRouter gives you access to many hosted models through one API. Creating an account and generating an API key costs nothing, and OpenRouter offers several :free-tagged models you can use at no charge (paid models are billed per-token only if you choose one later).

  1. Go to openrouter.ai and click Sign Up (GitHub, Google, or email — free).
  2. Once logged in, open openrouter.ai/keys.
  3. Click Create Key, give it a name (e.g. "FinAgent"), and click Create.
  4. Copy the key immediately — it's shown only once and starts with sk-or-....
  5. In FinAgent, choose OpenRouter as the LLM backend and paste the key into the OpenRouter API key field (Settings page, or the finagent --setup wizard).

items.title: Option C — Claude / Anthropic (cloud API — paid)
items.text:
Anthropic's Claude models give the highest categorization accuracy but require a billed API key — unlike OpenRouter, there is no free tier.

  1. Go to console.anthropic.com and sign up or log in.
  2. Add billing (required before the API will work): open Settings → Billing, add a payment method, and purchase API credits. Anthropic bills per token — check current rates at anthropic.com/pricing before heavy use.
  3. Open API Keys in the console sidebar and click Create Key. Name it (e.g. "FinAgent") and create it.
  4. Copy the key immediately — it's shown only once and starts with sk-ant-....
  5. In FinAgent, choose Claude as the LLM backend and paste the key into the Claude API key field. The default model is claude-opus-4-5; you can change it in the same form.

items.title: Where FinAgent stores things
items.text: Path Purpose ~/.finagent/config.json Your configuration (reference) Statements folder (you choose) Raw bank CSV/tabular statement exports (not PDFs) Processing folder (you choose) Pipeline output + dashboard data

items.title: Google Places API lookup
items.text: FinAgent can resolve a merchant's category from Google Places — a paid, high-accuracy alternative to the free OpenStreetMap lookup. This page covers what it does, how the request flow works, and what it costs.

items.title: Where it fits in the pipeline
items.text:
Every run resolves categories in this order:

rule engine  →  location lookup (this stage)  →  language model  →  merge

Location lookup itself has several interchangeable backends, selected by Settings → Location Engine for Categorization → Method. Google Places is one of them, alongside OpenStreetMap (Nominatim), Google Maps (Selenium, Dev only), and "off". Whichever merchants the location stage cannot resolve are passed on to the configured LLM.

items.title: The two Place API modes
items.text:
Method What it does place_api Calls Google Places for every merchant not already cached. Most accurate, calls Google most often. place_api_combined Tries the free OpenStreetMap lookup first; only calls Google Places when OpenStreetMap has no usable category. Fewer paid calls.

Both modes are available in the Personal profile — no need to switch to Dev.

items.title: Getting an API key
items.text:
1. In Google Cloud Console, enable Places API (New) on a project with billing enabled.
  2. Create an API key and (recommended) restrict it to the Places API.
  3. Paste the key into Settings → Google Places API key. It's masked after saving; leave the masked value alone to keep the existing key.

Full walkthrough

See Google's own guide: Get a Places API key — also linked directly from the Settings field.

items.title: How a match is decided
items.text:
Google Places results are matched conservatively rather than optimistically:

  • Only a fixed allowlist of specific Google place types (e.g. grocery_store, coffee_shop, gas_station) map to a FinAgent category. Broad types like store or point_of_interest are deliberately ignored — they're too vague to categorize safely.
  • The returned business name and the most specific location evidence available (an exact ZIP code, or a matching city/state) must agree with the statement text before a match is accepted.
  • Anything ambiguous, mismatched, or using an unmapped type is left uncategorized rather than guessed — it can still be picked up by the LLM stage or a manual rule.

items.title: Privacy and cost
items.text:
• FinAgent sends Google only the merchant query text and whatever location hint is available (ZIP, city, or state) — never transaction amounts, account numbers, or your name.
  • Requests run directly from your machine to Google; nothing is proxied through a FinAgent server.
  • Every resolved merchant is cached locally (each mode keeps its own cache), so the same merchant is only looked up once until the cache entry expires — this keeps repeat runs fast and avoids repeat billing.
  • Google Places is a paid API. Charges are billed by Google directly to the Google Cloud project tied to your key; FinAgent does not track or estimate your Google bill. Review Places API pricing before enabling it.
  • The Settings page flags this method with a 💵 "may cost money" badge next to the Location Engine section heading, so it's never a silent choice.

items.title: Configuration reference
items.text:
Key Values Notes location_lookup_method place_api · place_api_combined See Configuration reference for the full list of methods. google_places_api_key string Required by both Place API modes. Stored locally in config.json and masked by the dashboard API.

Related reading: Processing pipeline for how the location stage fits into a run, and Profiles for what's available in Personal versus Dev.

items.title: Processing pipeline
items.text: The Process page runs the full FinAgent pipeline: statement parsing → rule-based categorization → location lookup → LLM categorization → merge → dashboard data generation.

items.title: Running from the dashboard
items.text:
• No dates selected (default): processes everything available.
  • Date range: once a first run exists, the page shows the date range your data covers and lets you narrow a run with start/end date pickers.
  • Live progress: an overall progress bar plus sub-bars for location lookup and LLM categorization, with a collapsible run log.

Run defaults (LLM provider, lookup method) come from Settings — change them there, not on the Process page.

items.title: Advanced switches (terminal only)
items.text:
The remaining pipeline options are deliberately terminal-only features:

Flag Purpose --orgs boa,amex Limit the run to specific banks --month 2026-05 Process a single month --clean-data Delete generated temp/transaction data first --no-location-lookup Skip the location stage entirely --lookup-method nominatim\|none Override lookup method for one run --clear-lookup-cache Wipe the lookup cache before running --refresh-lookup-cache Ignore cached lookups, overwrite with fresh results

See Running from the terminal for the full command set.

items.title: Categorization stages
items.text:
Every transaction records how it was categorized in the categorization_stage column — and the Transactions page colors category tags accordingly:

Stage Meaning Color rule Deterministic keyword rule Blue location_lookup Resolved from merchant location data Teal llm:<provider> Categorized by the language model Violet user_defined Edited by you in the dashboard Orange merge Carried over from a previous run Gray uncategorized Nothing matched Red

items.title: Profiles: Personal & Dev
items.text: The dashboard has a profile toggle (top-right of the Settings page) with two modes. Personal is the default and what almost everyone should use.

items.title: Personal (default)
items.text:
Personal keeps the dashboard focused and privacy-first:

  • Location lookup offers Open Street Map, Place API, Place API combined flow, or off.
  • Place API modes require a billing-enabled Google Places API key. The combined flow tries OpenStreetMap first and calls Google only when OSM cannot derive a usable category. See Google Places API lookup for the full flow, matching rules, and cost details.
  • An optional checkbox lets you share a contact email with OpenStreetMap — purely voluntary feedback, off by default.
  • Selenium-based Google Maps lookup remains hidden in Personal.
  • Category editing is limited to what the pipeline supports safely.

items.title: Dev
items.text:
Dev mode unlocks maintainer features:

  • A separate development configuration that stays isolated from your personal data.
  • Google Maps Selenium lookup and its ChromeDriver options.
  • The Add category button on the Categories page (still discouraged — the category set is tuned for the rule engine and LLM prompts).

items.title: Activating Dev
items.text:
Flip the toggle to Dev on the Settings page and enter the password (finagent). FinAgent then loads the Dev configuration into the Settings form and shows its config-file path. This is only a preview until you press Save changes:

  • Save changes writes the displayed profile's settings and makes that profile active across the dashboard and subsequent Process runs.
  • Discard returns to the currently active profile without changing its configuration.
  • Switching back to Personal does not require a password, but it still waits for Save changes before activation.

Personal normally uses ~/.finagent/config.json; Dev normally uses ~/.finagent-dev/config.json. Each file retains its own folders, provider, API keys, and processing settings.

items.title: Terminal config profiles
items.text:
From the terminal, keep to the same two supported profiles used by the dashboard:

finagent --profile personal
finagent --profile dev

Each profile keeps its own folders, provider, and settings. See Running from the terminal.

The profile supplied at launch is initially active. Running finagent without --profile starts Personal; use --profile dev when Dev should be active immediately.

items.title: Development restart helper
items.text:
When dashboard/restart-server.sh starts with --profile and --config-dir, that custom config directory remains associated with the starting profile. Settings edits that exact file while the profile is selected. The other profile continues to use its normal config path.

An explicit --data-dir is a pinned development override and remains in use when profiles change. Without that override, activating a profile also changes the dashboard data and statements paths to those in the selected config.

items.title: Quick start
items.text: Choose one platform and run the shortest setup below. For prerequisites, security prompts, provider setup, persistence, updates, and troubleshooting, see Installation.

items.title: macOS
items.text:
Download FinAgent-<version>-macOS.dmg, then run:

open FinAgent-<version>-macOS.dmg
open /Applications/FinAgent.app

On the first launch, macOS may require Control-click → Open. Complete setup in the dashboard.

items.title: Linux x86_64
items.text:
Node.js 18+ must already be available. Download FinAgent-Linux-x86_64.tar.gz, then run:

tar -xzf FinAgent-Linux-x86_64.tar.gz
cd finagent_bundle
./install.sh
finagent

items.title: Windows x64
items.text:
Download FinAgent-Windows-x64.exe, then run it from PowerShell:

Start-Process .\FinAgent-Windows-x64.exe

Leave Launch FinAgent selected on the final installer page.

items.title: Docker
items.text:
Keep FinAgent-Docker-x86_64.tar.gz, docker_up.sh, and docker-compose.yml in the same folder, then run:

docker load -i FinAgent-Docker-x86_64.tar.gz
chmod +x docker_up.sh

./docker_up.sh \
  --statements "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/statements" \
  --processing "$HOME/Documents/FinAgent/processing" \
  --no-ollama-model

Open the dashboard at http://localhost:3001. Local documentation is at http://localhost:3003.

To download and select the included small Ollama model, replace --no-ollama-model with --ollama-model. See Docker installation for custom ports, models, Claude/OpenRouter, storage, updates, and troubleshooting.

items.title: Restarting FinAgent
items.text: Some Settings changes (dashboard port, folders) only take effect after a restart.

items.title: If you launched the app (DMG / binary)
items.text:
1. Quit: close the terminal window FinAgent opened, or press ++ctrl+c++ in it. On macOS you can also quit the FinAgent app from the Dock.
  2. Relaunch the app. The dashboard reopens in your browser on the configured port.

items.title: If you launched from the terminal
items.text:
# stop
Ctrl-C

# start again (skip reprocessing)
finagent --dashboard-only

items.title: If you launched with Docker
items.text:
Restart the existing container without changing its mounted data or settings:

docker restart finagent

To remove and recreate the container, run this from the folder containing docker-compose.yml, then repeat your normal ./docker_up.sh command:

docker compose --project-name finagent down

Statements, processing output, config, and downloaded Ollama models persist. See Docker installation for ports, providers, updates, and complete launcher examples.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• Port already in use — an old FinAgent process is still running:

    lsof -ti tcp:3000 | xargs kill    # replace 3000 with your port

  • Dashboard shows stale data — hard-refresh the browser (++cmd+shift+r++ on macOS, ++ctrl+shift+r++ elsewhere).

  • Changed folders in Settings — folders are locked after first-run setup; re-run finagent --setup from the terminal to move them safely.

items.title: First-run setup
items.text: The very first time you launch FinAgent (no ~/.finagent/config.json yet), the app starts the dashboard and opens the Settings page in setup mode. Every other page stays locked until setup is complete.

items.title: The three steps
items.text:
1. Folders — choose where your raw statements live and where processed data should go. FinAgent creates the bank subfolders (AMEX, BOA, CHASE, CITI, USBANK — each with CheckingAC and CreditAC) automatically when you complete setup.
  2. Categorization engine — pick an LLM provider (Ollama, OpenRouter, or Claude) and a location-lookup method. See Setting up an LLM provider for step-by-step instructions, including how to get a free OpenRouter key or a paid Claude key, and pulling a default Ollama model.
  3. Dashboard — pick the port the dashboard runs on.

Press Complete setup. The Import page unlocks immediately; the remaining pages unlock after your first processing run generates dashboard data. Import a CSV or supported tabular text export downloaded from your bank; PDF statements are not supported.

items.title: How pages unlock
items.text: State Unlocked pages No config yet Settings only Setup complete, no statements Settings, Import Statements imported, no dashboard data Settings, Import, Process Dashboard data exists Everything

items.title: Prefer the terminal?
items.text:
The classic terminal wizard is still there:

finagent --setup

See Running from the terminal for all flags.

items.title: Running from the terminal
items.text: Everything the dashboard does — and more — is available from the terminal. Use the finagent command after installation.

items.title: Everyday commands
items.text:
finagent                    # open the dashboard (default)
finagent --terminal         # open the interactive terminal menu
finagent --dashboard-only   # skip processing, just serve the dashboard
finagent --pipeline-only    # process data, don't start the dashboard
finagent --setup            # (re)run the interactive setup wizard
finagent --version          # print the version
finagent --help             # full flag reference

Running finagent without a switch now opens the dashboard directly and does not start processing or show the terminal menu. Use finagent --terminal when you want the numbered terminal options. Processing still runs when you pass a pipeline switch such as --orgs, or when you start it from the dashboard's Process page.

items.title: Pipeline switches
items.text:
finagent --orgs boa,amex            # only these banks
finagent --month 2026-05            # single month
finagent --start-date 2026-01-01 --end-date 2026-06-30
finagent --clean-data               # wipe generated temp data first
finagent --no-location-lookup       # rules + LLM only
finagent --lookup-method nominatim  # one-run lookup override
finagent --clear-lookup-cache       # wipe the lookup cache
finagent --refresh-lookup-cache     # re-resolve every location

If no statements are present, a terminal processing command starts the dashboard and opens its Import page instead of running the pipeline. Import a CSV or supported tabular text bank export there; PDF statements are not supported. The old desktop import window is no longer used.

Cloud API keys from the terminal

Keys entered in FinAgent Settings or finagent --setup are saved in your profile, so you do not need to export them again. If you select a cloud provider only with terminal options and have not saved its key, set the matching environment variable before starting FinAgent. The pipeline and the dashboard server inherit it.

macOS / LinuxWindows PowerShell 
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY="sk-or-your-key"
finagent --llm-provider open_router --orgs boa

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-your-key"
finagent --llm-provider claude --orgs boa

$env:OPENROUTER_API_KEY = "sk-or-your-key"
finagent --llm-provider open_router --orgs boa

$env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "sk-ant-your-key"
finagent --llm-provider claude --orgs boa

These commands set the key only for the current terminal session. Avoid putting API keys directly in commands that may be saved in shell history.

items.title: Maintenance
items.text:
finagent --overwrite-dashboard-data   # regenerate dashboard data from scratch
finagent --delete-dashboard-data      # remove dashboard data (asks first)
finagent --reset-all                  # factory reset config + data (asks first)
finagent --reset-all --with-statements  # ...including raw statements
finagent --yes                        # answer "yes" to confirmation prompts

items.title: Profiles from the terminal
items.text:
finagent --profile personal   # run with the personal profile
finagent --profile dev        # run with the dev profile

Only these two profiles are supported in the user-facing workflow right now. See Profiles for what the dashboard's Personal/Dev toggle does.

items.title: Dashboard view range
items.text:
finagent --dashboard-only --start-date 2026-01-01 --end-date 2026-03-31

Serves the dashboard restricted to that date window without reprocessing.
